page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with x86_64 architecture, presenting 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. It provides 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU memory allocation. The instance features 33 MB of shared L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector instructions alongside AES-NI cryptographic acceleration. Networking capabilities include a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while local disk storage is not bundled, necessitating attached cloud storage volumes for persistent data.

Synthetic performance profiles reflect architectural tradeoffs characteristic of older-generation Intel Xeon platforms. Single-threaded throughput is comparatively restricted, evidenced by low percentiles in single-core stress-ng tests and a Geekbench single-core score of 928.0. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics scale uniformly across all 16 vCPUs, producing an average multi-core score of 5773.0 in Geekbench and 11726.09 in multi-core stress-ng runs. Memory bandwidth delivers steady throughput, reaching 74.57 GB/sec read and 61.0 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks, supporting approximately 11.54 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-bound tasks that depend purely on single-core IPC, such as gzip compression, exhibit lower efficiency compared to aggregate throughput workloads.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, ecs.r5.4xlarge prioritizes memory density over cutting-edge per-core compute capability. By offering an extensive memory footprint relative to its 16 vCPUs without the overhead of integrated high-speed local NVMe, it provides predictable resource allocation for stateful memory-bound architectures. The server fits in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, intermediate-scale relational databases, big data batch extraction, ETL pipelines, and enterprise application backends requiring moderate concurrency and large memory overhead.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the KVM hypervisor, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor. Featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network capacity. Persistent local storage is omitted, relying on external network-attached volumes. In benchmark evaluations, multi-threaded operations and memory subsystems deliver consistent middle-tier throughput, registered by 11.54 million Redis SET operations per second and steady large-block uncached memory transfers of 74.57 GB/sec read and 61.0 GB/sec write. However, single-core processing metrics are subdued due to base processor clocking and instruction throughput limitations. Consequently, the configuration trades top-tier single-threaded compute speed for high RAM capacity, establishing it as an effective platform for in-memory caches, relational database management systems, data processing pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
